transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Is there anything you'd like to know about how you're getting on since your operation?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, yes, I do have some questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You can actually start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. 

However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise, and also avoid swimming for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. I also wanted to know when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure whether it's okay to use yours specifically, I'd suggest checking with your care team to be certain, as they'll know your full medical history.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I've noticed I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess this further. 

Are you experiencing mild sensitivity, or is it more severe with pain and redness?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's more of a mild sensitivity, and things just seem brighter than usual. I'll definitely try out wearing sunglasses more often. Thanks for the tip! I have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? That'll help me give you better advice about what to expect with your vision right now.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: The surgery was about two weeks ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Thank you for letting me know. At two weeks, some mild blurriness can still be normal as your eyes continue to settle. However, if your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

If you're concerned about how clear your vision is at this stage, it would be worth mentioning it to your care team so they can assess it for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that's all I needed to know for now. Thank you so much for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Just to confirm before we finish - have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.
